subject: Data Structures
title: Discover Linked Lists
description: Discover how nodes connect to form a Linked List.

mission.title: Discover the Chain
mission.description: Find out how one node connects to another.

quiz.question: After removing the first node, where does HEAD point?
options: The next node in the chain
The last node in the chain

discovery.title: Nodes Connected by Links
discovery.summary: A Linked List stores data in nodes where each node keeps a reference to another node.

sections.title: What is a Linked List?
sections.content: A Linked List stores items in a chain instead of placing them next to each other.

sections.title: Nodes
sections.content: Each item is stored in a node. A node holds data and information about the next node.

sections.title: Links and references
sections.content: A link, also called a reference, connects one node to the next node in the chain.

sections.title: Operations
sections.content: ADD creates a new node in the chain. REMOVE takes a node out and updates the link.

sections.title: Real-world example
sections.content: Think of a treasure hunt: each clue points to the next clue until the trail ends.

alternate_explanations.title: Think of linked train cars
alternate_explanations.content: A Linked List is like train cars connected in a chain. Each car carries its own value and is connected to the next car.

alternate_explanations.title: Follow the head
alternate_explanations.content: ADD 7, then ADD 14, creating 7 → 14. REMOVE takes away 7, so HEAD now points to 14.

introduction.title: Meet the Linked List
introduction.content: A Linked List stores items as separate nodes. Each node knows where the next node is, so the list forms a chain.
points: A link connects it to the next node.
You will build a chain and watch HEAD move.

worked_example.title: Watch a chain form
worked_example.content: Each new node connects to the end of the chain instead of taking a fixed position in an array.

steps.explanation: HEAD points to the first node.
The first node links to the new node.
Removing the first node makes HEAD follow its next link.

worked_example.conclusion: The nodes do not need to sit next to each other; their links keep the chain connected.

next.title: Build a chain below.
next.content: Add nodes, then remove the first one and watch HEAD change.

add: The first node becomes the place where HEAD starts.
A new node joins the chain through a next link.
The chain now has another connected node.
action_explanations.remove: The first node leaves, so HEAD follows the link to the next node.

challenge.title: Linked List Challenge
challenge.start_message: Build a short connected chain, then change where HEAD points.
challenge.continue_message: Challenge complete. Keep experimenting with links and HEAD.

phases.title: Build a three-node chain
phases.instruction: Create three connected nodes. Compare the chain in the playground with the target.
phases.feedback: A chain needs three added nodes before it matches the target.

phases.title: Move HEAD forward
phases.instruction: Remove the first node so HEAD points to the next node.

target.label: New target
target.description: HEAD starts at the second node in the original chain.

phases.feedback: Look at the first node and where HEAD should point next.

recall.title: Recall
recall.prompt: In your own words, how does a Linked List keep its nodes connected?
recall.empty_message: Write a short explanation before submitting.
recall.model_answer: Each node stores a link or reference to the next node. Following those links lets the list form a chain from HEAD to null.

guidance.start_message: Build the requested chain from HEAD to null.

items.content: ADD appends a node; HEAD remains at the first node.

phases.title: Build a chain
phases.feedback: Follow the nodes from HEAD to null.

guidance.start_message: Transform the linked list without being told each button.

items.content: REMOVE moves HEAD forward; ADD attaches a node at the tail.

phases.title: Transform the chain
phases.feedback: Compare the HEAD node and tail node with the target.

guidance.start_message: Reach the target chain using at most three list operations.

phases.title: Solve the list puzzle
phases.instruction: Transform START into TARGET in three operations or fewer.
phases.feedback: Only the HEAD node can be removed directly.

constraints.operation_limit_message: Operation limit reached. Retry with a shorter plan.

guidance.start_message: Work with an unfamiliar chain independently.

phases.title: Master an unfamiliar chain
phases.instruction: Transform the randomized list into the target structure.
phases.feedback: Trace from HEAD and compare every next link with the target.

thinking.title: Think through the links
thinking.instruction: Track which node becomes HEAD and which node becomes the tail before the replay.
thinking.do_not_execute: Do not modify the list yet. Follow the links mentally.

prediction_fields.label: Final nodes (HEAD → tail)
prediction_fields.prompt: Which node values remain in the chain?

prediction_fields.label: Next REMOVE value
prediction_fields.prompt: Which HEAD value would REMOVE take next?

solve.title: Expert Linked List
solve.instruction: Transform START into TARGET with no hints. Reason from HEAD and tail.
solve.operation_rule: ADD changes the tail; REMOVE changes HEAD.
solve.feedback: Check which end each list operation changes.
solve.solved_result: You completed the randomized linked-list transformation.
